fields.habitat: Restricted to upland rainforest in north-eastern Queensland, from the Cooktown area towards Townsville. Records are concentrated in cooler forest at elevation.
fields.voice: Its varied voice includes twittering contact sounds, melodious sliding whistles and occasional rougher notes.

fields.habitat: Strongly associated with sandstone country, especially cliffs, escarpments and exposed rock ledges. River gorges provide characteristic places to look for this shrikethrush.

source.label: Michael Dahlem — Sandstone Shrike-thrush field observations

fields.identification: Adults develop a prominent casque on the bill. Younger birds can lack this feature, which can complicate their identification.

Adults have a light grey forehead and a greyish crown with diffuse dark streaks. Juveniles have a browner forehead and crown without the adult streaking. Adult males and females cannot be reliably separated by plumage or the listed measurements.

source.label: Australian Bird Study Association — Slaty-backed Thornbill

fields.identification: Males combine a black face and throat with a white eyebrow and throat-side patch, a grey breast and spotted flanks. Females have an ochre throat patch instead of a black throat.
fields.behaviour: Usually encountered alone or in pairs, sometimes in small family groups. It can remain motionless among forest-floor cover before suddenly flushing when approached closely.

fields.identification: The Australian Museum’s comparison of the western form describes males with a white abdomen, a yellow undertail, and paler upperparts and wings than the eastern form. Females have a smaller crest and an olive-green throat.
